claims.text: The starting powder mixture is nominally equiatomic CoCrFeNiTi.
As-cast or as-mixed CoCrFeNiTi has high porosity.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi has hardness below 350 HV.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling produces high lattice strain.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling sufficiently refines the grains.
The milling-induced strain and grain refinement lower the free-energy or activation barrier for an FCC-to-BCC solid-solution transition.
SPS at 1000°C produces near-theoretical densification.
SPS at 1000°C avoids excessive Ti-driven HCP precipitation.
The VEC must remain above a critical threshold for FCC stability.
Managing atomic-radius mismatch suppresses Laves-phase formation.
Mechanical alloying introduces a high dislocation density.
The thermal energy supplied by short-duration SPS is sufficient for diffusion and densification.
Ti-rich HCP phases are thermodynamically favored at higher temperatures or longer thermal-treatment durations.
High strain energy and grain-boundary density stabilize a metastable FCC/BCC solid-solution state.
VEC and atomic-radius mismatch govern the relevant phase-stability window.
The resulting alloy will have porosity below 2%.
The resulting microstructure will be dominant BCC or a strained FCC/BCC mixture.
The resulting alloy will exceed 400 HV and be significantly harder than cast counterparts.
The hardness increase will arise primarily from Hall-Petch grain-boundary strengthening rather than precipitation hardening.
Sintering above approximately 1050°C triggers excessive grain growth or decomposition into Ti-rich HCP or Laves phases.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires VEC to remain above a critical threshold for FCC stability while simultaneously positing an FCC-to-BCC transition and a dominant BCC outcome, without explaining how BCC becomes favored under the stated FCC-stability condition.

The central hypothesis specifies an FCC-to-BCC transition, but the mechanism alternatively proposes stabilization of strained FCC and the outcome permits either dominant BCC or an FCC/BCC mixture, leaving the claimed specific transition internally underdetermined.
